format: {name, note, instructable, clients?, expect: {stub, reason?}}. `instructable` is the raw object a Pond serves as an ask's payload. stub true means the client shows the ask only as an update stub, with Skip and nothing else; reason says why. pondStub: the Pond's own stub for a client too old to read a correction, recognised by its exact why ("This ask was corrected after it was posted. Update Hook to see the corrected steps; don't press Done here.") and its single step (do "Update Hook: menu bar › Check for Updates…"), as kind stub of revision-vectors.json writes it. unknownKey:<path>: the first key in document order that the client does not know, at a path such as steps[2].substeps[0].shell. unknownDone:<value>: a done value the client does not know, checked after every key. Known keys: ask v title why warning urgency steps verify reply done links from; step, sub-step and verify do where detail code lang expect url substeps question blocking warning optional required id file; question prompt choices multi; choice object label text; reply prompt choices; link label url path; from session host cwd. Known done values: steps reply message. The Swift core has no unknown-key check yet, so every unknownKey and unknownDone case, and the stub-false cases there only to contrast with them, carry clients ["android"] and a hand-written expect.
